statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. All 24 published hours fall inside the scheduled weekend halt of CME equity-index futures and the NAS100 CFD, so no pathological Nasdaq-100 price path can form within the window, while the macro backdrop behind elevated Stress stays unresolved.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold for every published hour because no tradable Nasdaq-100 venue exists before Sunday 22:00Z, which is beyond the final slot. Elevated Stress describes the 5.165% 10-year yield, $92.41 WTI and an unaccepted Iranian Hormuz proposal rather than any observed mean-reversion failure. Reopen gap risk falls outside this window.
headline: Nasdaq-100 inside the scheduled CME weekend closure after an orderly Friday advance; Tail at its floor with Stress elevated on 5.165% long-end yields, $92 crude and unresolved Hormuz diplomacy
body: Friday's session closed in orderly, two-sided fashion and nothing has traded since. Cash NDX finished 30,608.14, up 0.42% or 129.28 points, inside a 30,413.59-30,667.56 range and about 0.19% below the session high, while NQ Dec-26 was last 30,921.75, up 0.50%, within a 30,679.00-30,997.25 range and roughly 0.24% below its high. VIX fell 5.11% to 14.87 in a 14.68-15.94 range. All three major US averages posted weekly gains, the Dow up 0.93% to 51,828.62 and snapping a three-week losing streak, the S&P 500 up 0.51% to 7,743.41 and the Nasdaq Composite up 0.48% to 27,068.72. Retracements occurred repeatedly through the session and the index did not hold an extreme into the close, so none of the mean-reversion-failure amplifiers were present when the tape stopped. CME equity-index futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, which is more than twenty hours past the final published hour, so every slot in this assessment sits inside a scheduled closure with no tradable venue. That is why Tail is held at its floor rather than inferred from Friday's mildly positive tone. The environment behind elevated Stress is genuinely unresolved. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.165% after a 4bp Friday easing, having reached its highest level since the global financial crisis during the week, with H.15 showing the 2-year at 4.87% and the 30-year at 5.47%. The Federal Reserve raised rates 25bp on September 16 and futures price a 60-70% probability of a further increase in October. WTI settled at $92.41, down 2.33%, and Brent at $104.32, down 2.14%, leaving WTI about 7.4% lower on the week after Iran's foreign minister proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz within seven days in exchange for lifting the naval blockade, unfreezing assets and ending the conflict. President Trump has not accepted those terms and has ruled out lifting the blockade first, so the Hormuz closure and its supply premium remain in place. The coming week carries August PCE and final Q2 GDP on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and September payrolls on Friday with consensus near +100,000 and a 4.2% unemployment rate. Those are forward checkpoints that raise Stress and shape Confidence; under this contract they do not by themselves raise Tail before a price path is observed. Shared Finviz context was read and is 155 minutes old with collectionStatus partial and both its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was treated as stale supporting context only and contributed nothing to this assessment; all levels above come from primary sources verified directly.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 published hours the Claude state ranged between Tail 9 and 22 and never approached the block threshold. The overnight and early European stretch held Tail at 17-18 in normal conditions, three trend-up prints appeared between 06:00Z and 11:00Z as the index worked higher, and the US cash session settled into mixed conditions at Tail 18-21. The 13:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable rather than reconstructed. The final four hours fell to Tail 12, 10, 10 and 9 as CME futures settled into the weekend closure and no tradable price path remained. Stress stayed in the 47-59 band throughout on the long-end yield and oil backdrop, and Confidence held between 85 and 88.
outlookSummary: The entire published window falls inside the scheduled CME weekend closure: futures settled at 21:00Z on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, at least twenty-two hours past the final slot. Tail is held between 9 and 10 for all 24 hours because sustained mean-reversion failure requires a tradable price path, and none of the inherited amplifiers, shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, or an index pinned near an extreme, can be observed while every Nasdaq-100 venue is shut. Stress eases from 46 to 45 through the deepest part of the closure and firms to 50 by the final hour as the PCE, ISM and payrolls week and a live October rate decision approach. Confidence decays from 85 to 71 across the window because later hours sit progressively further from the verified Friday evidence set, while the exchange calendar anchoring the low Tail stays certain. Weekend geopolitical or diplomatic developments would transmit only as headlines within this window; their earliest possible price expression is the Sunday reopen, which lies outside it.
